suread: review R1 素读（只读 text/，未开 md）

facts.fact: 时间锚：Henri 派对后的那个周一；她醒来一身汗随即发抖
facts.anchor: The Monday after Henri’s party, I woke drenched in sweat, then immediately began to shiver

facts.fact: 外窗挂着水珠；电视里气象员对 Amelia Island 和 Jacksonville 发高温警报，屋里却冷得刺骨
facts.anchor: A weatherman on TV announced heat advisories in Amelia Island and Jacksonville, but inside the house, it was frigid

facts.fact: Virginia 的缺席在 Greer House 留下印子，但和她预想的不同：像屋子的气氛扩张过来，占掉她留下的空位
facts.anchor: it was like its atmosphere expanded, taking up the space she’d left behind

facts.fact: 她边半听新闻边把梦画下来
facts.anchor: I half listened to the news as I sketched out my dream

facts.fact: 梦：她站在没踝深的 marsh 水里，捡起脚边的步枪，那只温柔的手把枪引上她的肩
facts.anchor: Ankle-deep in marsh water, I’d picked up the rifle at my feet, and that gentle hand had guided it to my shoulder

facts.fact: 那只看不见的存在替她摆好瞄准姿势时，她抗拒着，怕和挫败让她发抖
facts.anchor: As the invisible being had positioned me to aim, I’d resisted, shaking with fear and frustration

facts.fact: 在书桌前她仍觉得那双眼睛在自己背上，每次回头都没人
facts.anchor: At my desk, I still felt those eyes on me, though each time I turned, I found no one

facts.fact: 到办公室时汗已浸额头；Nova 举着手持风扇迎客，睫毛膏晕到下眼睑，神色依旧平静
facts.anchor: Nova greeted us with a handheld fan pointed at her face. Mascara bled onto her lower eyelids, but her expression remained placid

facts.fact: Nova 说：空调坏了；冰箱冰柜塞了瓶装水，不够她再去买
facts.anchor: “AC’s down,” she said

facts.fact: 令她意外，Nova 打断了 Gazzie 的话——高温显然把 Nova 从前的拘束剥掉了
facts.anchor: To my surprise, Nova cut her off. The heat had apparently stripped away any restraint she’d shown before

facts.fact: Nova 转述：Harrison 在后面和修理工一起，估计要修一整天；他不想有人当「后排技术指导」
facts.anchor: He also said he’d rather not have any backseat technicians.”

facts.fact: 她的私念：好，那就不用马上见 Harrison
facts.anchor: Good. I wouldn’t have to see him right away

facts.fact: Gazzie 嘴张开又合上再张开——Nova 的插话也惊到了她；她说自己去 slaughter
facts.anchor: Nova’s interruption had surprised her, too. “I’ll be in slaughter.”

facts.fact: Nova 更大声更慢地重复：里面很热——像对听力不好的人说话
facts.anchor: Nova spoke louder and more slowly, like Gazzie was hard of hearing

facts.fact: Nova 朝她交代：你的窗能开，卡住就晃一晃
facts.anchor: “Your window opens. Give it a jiggle if it’s stuck.”

facts.fact: 她想起那批发霉的档案——先前被尸骸的事分了心没提——说：我们有个麻烦
facts.anchor: “Actually,” I said, remembering the moldy files. I’d been too distracted by the carcasses to mention them before. “We’ve got a problem.”

facts.fact: Gazzie 听完整份报告直皱眉，尤其听到霉是一夜之间长出来的；但她另有安排：Joe 说 kudzu 又爬上蛋库了，你去处理
facts.anchor: “Joe says the kudzu’s back on the egg barn. Deal with it.”

facts.fact: 她心里的盘算：太好了——若 Joe 在外面，就能审他，确认抛尸那天早上他是否真的在剥皮
facts.anchor: If Joe was outside, I’d be able to interrogate him, confirm whether he’d really been skinning the morning the carcasses were dumped

facts.fact: 她自标这一步的性质：证明背后是人的最后一把、孤注一掷的尝试
facts.anchor: A last, desperate attempt to prove a human was behind it all

facts.fact: 她带着大剪刀和除草剂开高尔夫球车去蛋库；一路目视前方，防着 Harrison 在路两边——他并没在
facts.anchor: Loppers and herbicide in tow, I drove a golf cart to the egg barn, keeping my head straight in case Harrison was on either side of the road, which he wasn’t

facts.fact: 走近蛋库她惊得张嘴：周五路过时它还和别的库房一样——两倍大、完全空着，七八月起要在里面孵蛋
facts.anchor: it was twice as large and completely empty; we’d start hatching eggs inside in July and August

facts.fact: 这天早上，绿藤把整栋建筑缠死了；藤从蛋库鼓出来，像一件宽松的衬衫
facts.anchor: green vines choked the entire building

facts.fact: （另一段）藤从蛋库鼓出来，像一件宽松的衬衫
facts.anchor: puffed out from the barn like a loose blouse

facts.fact: 她绕到库后很快找到源头：kudzu 一路直通东边五十码的沼泽——猎场；据 Nova 说，富游客付钱来杀自己的鳄鱼和野猪
facts.anchor: Kudzu trailed directly to the swamp fifty yards to the east—the hunting grounds, where, according to Nova, wealthy tourists paid to kill their own gators and wild pigs

facts.fact: kudzu 一个周末就蔓延了那么远；热浪压肩，她盯着眼前的怪物，头昏涨
facts.anchor: The kudzu had spread that far over the weekend

facts.fact: 她的判断：kudzu 素来凶，但没凶到这个地步；而且只缠了蛋库这一栋——像选定唯一目标，像在传话
facts.anchor: Kudzu was aggressive, but not that aggressive. And it hadn’t covered any building other than the egg barn, like it had chosen a single target, like it was sending a message

facts.fact: 她给那条「消息」配上内容：它不想农场再养出一年的鳄鱼来杀
facts.anchor: It didn’t want the farm growing another year’s worth of alligators for slaughter

facts.fact: 两个短句定性：这不正常。这是 Ironheart
facts.anchor: This was not normal.

facts.fact: 念头一出她逼自己笑：是热昏头了；Greer 家运气差归差，神话生物不会像魔术师一样让藤一夜长成
facts.anchor: The heat was getting to me. Sure, we Greers had bad luck, but a mythical creature wasn’t making vines grow overnight like a magician

facts.fact: 可念头不散，边剪边在脑子里回响：Ironheart 三连；她自嘲真的要疯了——下一步该看见 Ida 戴着老式卷发筒出现在浴室里
facts.anchor: Ironheart. Ironheart. Ironheart. I really was losing it, I mused. Next, I’d see Ida in my bathroom, hair in old-fashioned curlers

facts.fact: Nova 的操作指示：贴地剪掉再喷药；她几分钟就进了节奏，但每一剪都是角力——藤像笼中豹寸土必争
facts.anchor: each cut was a struggle, the plant fighting me for every inch it gave, like a panther resisting the confines of a cage

facts.fact: 她不时抬头盼 Joe 出现，没等到；剪到半栋库房时衬衫已被汗浸透
facts.anchor: Every so often, I’d look up, hoping to find Joe, with no luck

facts.fact: 她退到休息室拿了瓶温水，趁 Nova 座位空着溜到正门外，背靠门边墙坐下——那里正好有荫
facts.anchor: Retreating to the break room, I grabbed a bottle of lukewarm water and made my way to the front office

facts.fact: 一句人声：真恶心
facts.anchor: “It’s disgusting.”

facts.fact: 后颈皮肤刺麻——她认得这声音，是 Nova
facts.anchor: The skin on the back of my neck prickled. I knew that voice. It was Nova

facts.fact: 睁眼费劲；水泥地热气像蒸汽上蒸；视野里没有 Nova
facts.anchor: Heat radiated from the cement, waves of it rising like steam. She wasn’t anywhere in sight

facts.fact: 她判定声音来自楼左侧；探头没人，声音反而更响；没有车可藏、没有垃圾桶
facts.anchor: Listening hard, I determined her voice was coming from the left of the building

facts.fact: 一只空塑料水瓶从天上落下，在水泥地上弹跳
facts.anchor: An empty plastic water bottle fell from the sky, bouncing on the concrete

facts.fact: 头顶：办公室二层唯一会议室的窗支开着；Nova 坐在窗台上，侧对她、电话贴耳、右手夹烟，烟灰簌簌往下掉
facts.anchor: Above me, on the office’s second floor, a window to the sole meeting room was propped open. Nova sat on the sill, her side to me, phone to her ear, cigarette in her right hand

facts.fact: 她听到的电话内容：她简直是在拿砸烂他们的头取乐，或者说减压什么的；我知道你知道，可我说，搞什么鬼？
facts.anchor: “She’s literally bashing their heads in for fun or stress relief or whatever.”

facts.fact: 电话里最关键的一句：对，我没锁
facts.anchor: “Yeah. I left it unlocked.”

facts.fact: 电话收尾：一声少女似的笑——「那我就不客气了」
facts.anchor: A final pause and a girlish giggle. “I’ll take you up on that.”

facts.fact: Nova 把手机从耳边拿开，盯着屏幕看了几秒才搁到腿上
facts.anchor: She pulled the phone away from her ear and looked at the screen for several seconds before setting it on her lap

facts.fact: 她绕回角落，脑子比一整天任何时候都清楚
facts.anchor: I snuck around the corner again, mind clearer than it had been all day

facts.fact: 她立论：Nova 参与了破坏案——她太另类，不适合农场（流苏背心、大豆蜡烛）；她来上班就是为了接近这里
facts.anchor: She was too alternative to work on a farm. Not with her fringed vests and soy candles. She’d taken the job to get access

facts.fact: 她推论：Nova 必是某种活动家；且从电话加刀阵加抛尸看，并非单干——Joe 必是同伙，这解释了他的不在场证明
facts.anchor: Based on the call—not to mention the planted knives and dumped carcasses—she wasn’t working alone, either. Joe must be her accomplice; that explained his alibis

facts.fact: 她心里有一半知道答案没这么简单：Joe 对女性的公开蔑视，配一个被宠坏的 Gen Z 姑娘？
facts.anchor: Given Joe’s open disdain for women, I couldn’t imagine he’d work with a pampered Gen Z girl

facts.fact: 更深的那一半 weighs 着同步的幼鳄、藻类、霉、kudzu——没有一样是人能编排的
facts.anchor: An even deeper part of me weighed the in-sync juvenile alligators, the algae, the mold, the kudzu, understanding that none of that could be orchestrated by a human

facts.fact: 她承认自欺的动机：她想要局面简单——想做一个能在一下午里解决家族凡人麻烦的体面人——于是逼自己信
facts.anchor: But I wanted the situation to be straightforward—wanted to be a decent person who could solve her family’s mundane, not-supernatural problems in an afternoon—so I forced myself to believe it was

facts.fact: 她心跳如鼓走回楼里；怕晕倒在见到 Nova 之前，一步一步爬楼梯；发短信约 Gazzie 来二层
facts.anchor: I considered jogging up the staircase but didn’t want to faint before I confronted Nova. Taking the steps one by one, I texted Gazzie to meet me on the second floor

facts.fact: 她冲进会议室时 Nova 还坐在窗台上
facts.anchor: Nova was still sitting in the window when I burst inside the meeting room

facts.fact: Nova 翻白眼：修理工还没给我更新，有消息我会告诉你
facts.anchor: She rolled her eyes. “The repairman hasn’t updated me. I’ll tell you when he does.”

facts.fact: 她喘着气说 Gazzie 在路上，试着借来对方的底气
facts.anchor: “Gazzie’s on her way,” I panted, trying to channel her confidence

facts.fact: Nova：那我反正也变不出别的说法
facts.anchor: “Well, I can’t tell her anything different.”

facts.fact: 她：她来不是为了这个
facts.anchor: “That’s not what she’s coming for.”

facts.fact: 她摊牌：我听见你了
facts.anchor: “I heard you.”

facts.fact: Nova 抿唇警觉：听见我什么
facts.anchor: Nova pursed her lips, alert. “Heard me what?”

facts.fact: 她列举罪状：动物尸骸？恶心。插刀那手只是怪。毁皮我能理解，但放跑一条鳄鱼？它本可能从我腿上咬掉一块
facts.anchor: Ruining the skins I can understand, but letting an alligator loose? It could have taken a chunk out of my leg.

facts.fact: Nova 打量她；她表情里的得意多半出卖了她；Nova 说：你又没受伤——头靠上窗框，一副松弛到家的样子
facts.anchor: “You didn’t get hurt,” she said, resting her head against the window frame. The picture of ease.

facts.fact: 她：我可能受伤。Nova：可你没有（两句对答）
facts.anchor: “But you didn’t.”

facts.fact: 会议室一股陈味，像微波炉内部
facts.anchor: The room smelled stale, like the inside of a microwave

facts.fact: 她追问图什么：是在给哪条宠物鳄鱼报仇吗
facts.anchor: “Are you avenging a pet alligator or something?”

facts.fact: Nova 皱眉反问：什么？她接不上话——「所以你是在抗议？」对方只重复：抗议？
facts.anchor: “Protesting?”

facts.fact: 她不耐烦地挑明：农场。你在 PETA 吗
facts.anchor: “The farm. Are you in PETA?”

facts.fact: Nova 脸上掠过恍然：哦，Dart——这不是抗议
facts.anchor: “Oh, Dart,” she said. “It’s not a protest.”

facts.fact: 单凭那个同情的表情她就明白自己错了：Nova 不是活动家；对方是在可怜她消息不灵
facts.anchor: From her sympathetic expression alone, I understood I’d been mistaken. She wasn’t an activist

facts.fact: 她问那为什么做
facts.anchor: “Then why do it?”

facts.fact: Nova 慢慢摇头：关于你祖母，你并不知道一切
facts.anchor: “You don’t know everything about your grandmother.”

facts.fact: 她差点笑出 Nova 的拖延，追问什么意思
facts.anchor: I almost laughed at her stalling. “What’s that supposed to mean?”

facts.fact: Nova 的判词：她是个杀人犯。而且她别想再逍遥下去——不会再有了
facts.anchor: “She’s a killer. And she’s not getting away with it. Not anymore.”

facts.fact: 她的反应：嘴张开、唇黏在牙上，想不出一个字的回答；祖母当然是 killer——她每天杀几十条鳄鱼；可 Nova 为什么说得像启示、像警告
facts.anchor: Of course my grandmother was a killer—she killed dozens of alligators every day. But why did Nova say it like that? Like a revelation? A warning?

facts.fact: Leon 的那行字第三次浮上来：我要让她放我走，不成功便成仁
facts.anchor: I’ll make her let me go or die trying.

facts.fact: Nova 一个箭步跃下窗台、从她身边挤过去；她失去平衡、被热耗尽，向后摔倒，尾椎砸在地毯上，惊得几秒动弹不得
facts.anchor: Nova launched herself off the windowsill and pushed past me. Off balance and exhausted from the heat, I fell backward

facts.fact: Nova 消失后一口气没喘匀，Gazzie 已经朝她跑来，衬衫前襟一大片深褐——血，比平时多
facts.anchor: Gazzie was running toward me, a dark brown stain across her button-down. Blood. More than usual

facts.fact: 一阵失控的念头：她伤到 Nova 了？在走廊捅了她？用鳄鱼棒打晕了她？
facts.anchor: For a wild moment, I thought she’d hurt Nova. Stabbed her in the hallway. Bludgeoned her with the alligator bat

facts.fact: Gazzie 说我在我在，用一个惊人地像祖母的动作把手覆上她的额头
facts.anchor: In a shockingly grandmotherly move, she held her hand to my forehead

facts.fact: 她的猜想：那天早上把她吓着时按住她的冷手，也许就是 Gazzie——若破坏是人干的，Greer House 的怪事也许也是
facts.anchor: Maybe she was the one who’d pressed her cold hand to me that morning I got spooked; if the vandalism was caused by a human, maybe Greer House’s oddities were, too

facts.fact: 心刚鼓起来又一沉：Gazzie 指甲缝里有红褐色的血
facts.anchor: My heart swelled, then skipped as I noticed red-brown blood under her nails

facts.fact: 她盯着衬衫强问：出什么事了；Gazzie 烦躁地顺着她的视线看去：我在 slaughter——你到底需不需要帮忙
facts.anchor: “I was in slaughter. Do you or do you not need help?”

facts.fact: 误会揭开：Gazzie 以为她发短信是叫人扶她起来；她挥手朝门：她要走了
facts.anchor: She thought I’d texted her to help me stand up

facts.fact: Gazzie 问谁、去哪；她答：一切都是她在背后操办
facts.anchor: “She’s behind everything.”

facts.fact: Gazzie 双眼一亮，冲出房间；她数着十拍把气吐出来再吸回去，压心跳
facts.anchor: Gazzie’s eyes lit up, and she barreled out of the room. I held my breath for a ten count

facts.fact: 她的自评：成了——问清 Nova 就能查清农场的乱摊子，Gazzie 就会指定她做继承人
facts.anchor: We’d question Nova and get to the bottom of the farm mess, and Gazzie would name me heir

facts.fact: 末句：她只需要忘掉 Nova 告诉她的那些话
facts.anchor: I just had to forget what Nova had told me
